previous_description: Interactive element that triggers actions (button, menu, link, voice command)
definition: A user-operable control (button, hyperlink, menu entry, icon button or spoken command) whose activation starts an operation, a navigation or a state change. It is the trigger point that user input reaches, as opposed to the input fields, display components or layout containers around it.

distinguish_from.when: you are modelling the reusable trigger-plus-feedback behaviour (e.g. confirm-and-delete) that many controls share, rather than one concrete control in the interface
the symbol is the generic, reusable Button/Link/Menu definition in a design system with a props schema, rather than a specific control that triggers a specific action
the element is a configured placement of a non-action library component (table, chart, display, input) inside a View or SubView
you are modelling the state-machine edge that the activation causes (trigger event, destination state, guard), not the control the user operates

standard_reference: HTML 5.3 interactive content: the button element, the a element with href, and the menu element
code_evidence: A <button>, <a href> or design-system <Button>/<IconButton>/<Link> element rendered in a template with an onClick/onSelect/@click handler or a router 'to' target
A menu or toolbar configuration array whose entries carry a label, icon and handler or command id (e.g. items: [{label:'Delete', icon:'trash', onClick: ...}])
A voice or chat intent or command registration (e.g. an Alexa intent handler or a slash-command definition) that maps an utterance to an action invocation

attribute_descriptions.name: label
attribute_descriptions.description: The visible text or accessible name of the control (the button text, link text or spoken phrase). Set it whenever the control is not icon-only; for icon-only controls, set it to the aria-label value.

attribute_descriptions.name: icon
attribute_descriptions.description: Identifier of the icon displayed on the control, as a design-system icon name or asset path (e.g. 'trash', 'mdi-plus'). Set it when the control shows a glyph.

attribute_descriptions.name: disabled
attribute_descriptions.description: When true, the control is rendered but cannot be activated, corresponding to the HTML disabled attribute or aria-disabled. Set it only when the control is statically disabled; state-dependent disabling belongs on ExperienceState.disabledComponents.

attribute_descriptions.name: tooltip
attribute_descriptions.description: Short helper text shown on hover or focus, corresponding to the HTML title attribute or a tooltip component. Set it when the control's purpose is not obvious from its label or icon.

notes: The validations attribute fits poorly: HTML Constraint Validation applies to form-associated input controls, not buttons or links, and the layer has no input-field type to hold it. The style values 'link' and 'icon' duplicate the type values 'link' and 'icon-button'. 'menu' is a container of actions and arguably needs child items. The renders→librarycomponent relationship blurs the type/instance boundary.
